wire.headline: Northbridge Press Group Cuts 1,200 UK Jobs in Major Restructuring
sentences: Northbridge Press Group has announced the elimination of 1,200 jobs across its UK titles.
The company stated that this restructuring aims to save 45m GBP annually by 2026.
CEO Alan Thorne cited the digital shift as the primary driver for these changes.
Shares dropped 12% in pre-market trading following the announcement.
The redundancies will affect print divisions in Manchester and Leeds.
The consultation period is set to end on 15 October before final decisions are made.

PD.headline: Glasgow Newsroom Faces Closure Amid Digital Shift

sentences.text: Northbridge Press Group has announced that 1,200 jobs across its UK titles will be eliminated.
The Glasgow office is scheduled to close entirely by the end of November.
Workers at the Clyde facility have received immediate redundancy notices.
The primary driver for these changes was cited by CEO Alan Thorne as the digital shift.
The local council has offered a 5m GBP grant to support digital training initiatives.

sentences.fact: Community radio station partners with surviving newsroom staff
sentences.text: A community radio station has entered into a partnership with the surviving newsroom staff.

ND.headline: Northbridge Restructuring Sparks Union Ballot and Leadership Resignation

sentences.text: The company announced that the restructuring aims to save 45m GBP annually by 2026.
Alan Thorne, the head executive, identified the move toward digital as the main cause behind such modifications.
Unite the Union plans to ballot 8,500 members on strike action in response.
Analyst Sarah Jenkins called the cost savings insufficient for a turnaround.
Local MP David Croft demanded an inquiry into the potential job losses.
A reader group called Ink & Paper launched a petition for digital access.
Northbridge acquired the rival Daily Echo in 2019 for 300m GBP.
Print runs at the Deeside facility are set to halve by next quarter.
Editor-in-chief Marian Holt resigned, citing creative differences.
Digital subscription revenue grew only 2% last fiscal year.
Staff morale surveys show that 70% fear redundancy in the next 6 months.
